messages:
ops-bot: Pager triggered — elevated error rate in EU embeddings pipeline (P1). Notifying on-call @jen.
jen: I'm taking this. Quick triage: spike of 5xx/502s on embedding workers, looks correlated with KV cache misses and some node I/O errors.
mike: I didn't deploy anything in EU in the last 30m. Autoscaler shows thrash on eu-dedicated pool, some nodes reporting OOM/killed. Adding riley for infra.
riley: I see repeated NFS I/O timeouts from eu-srv-3. Restarting container on that host drops error rate for a minute then it climbs. I'm going to cordon eu-srv-3 and drain tasks.
jen: Ok — mitigation plan: 1) drain faulty host, 2) rebalance traffic to fallback embedding model (quantized small) to reduce memory pressure, 3) scale up healthy workers in EU. We need a customer-facing note. Drafting minimal initial status below.
jen: ```Initial update (now): We are investigating an issue affecting embeddings requests in the EU region. Some requests are returning errors or experiencing elevated latency. Our engineers are rebalancing traffic and routing requests to fallback capacity to reduce impact. Customers using EU endpoints may see intermittent failures or higher latency. We will provide further updates as we have more information. For urgent support, contact support@redwood.com.```
cathy: Good start. Add a short reassurance about customer data — "no data exfiltration" — and a line for Dedicated customers who might have isolated capacity.
legal: Suggest wording change: use "intermittent failures" instead of "errors" and avoid committing to an exact ETA. Also add support contact and a short line about data integrity.
jen: Updated draft per legal and cs/product. ```Update (posted): We are investigating an issue causing intermittent failures for embeddings requests in the EU region. Impact: a subset of EU requests may experience failures (5xx) or higher latency. Mitigation: traffic is being routed to fallback capacity and engineers are rebalancing workers; we are replacing an affected host. Dedicated customers with EU-dedicated pools: please contact your account rep if you see impact. No customer data was accessed or exfiltrated. We will provide further updates in approximately 30 minutes or as we learn more. For urgent support contact support@redwood.com.```
sam: Recommend explicitly calling out affected timeframe window once we have it and noting whether API/embedding tokens are impacted — otherwise 👍
cathy: LGTM :thumbsup:
jen: Posting now to status page.
ops-bot: Status update published: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/3187654321 — initial update posted.
mike: Continuing mitigation: replacing eu-srv-3, scaling +2 workers, temporarily bumping retry budget on the router for embeddings to reduce client-visible failures. Monitoring token pipeline and error rates.
riley: After host replacement and draining, error rate decreased to baseline. Root cause looks like an NFS kernel-level stall causing worker processes to block under load; escalating to eng-infra for postmortem.
jen: Verified: 5xx rate back to normal as of 3187654370 (UTC). Drafting resolved notice.
jen: ```Resolved: The issue affecting embeddings in the EU region has been resolved. Host eu-srv-3 exhibited I/O stalls causing intermittent failures; the host was replaced and workers rebalanced. Error rates have returned to normal. No customer data was exposed. If you continue to see issues, contact support@redwood.com and reference incident 3187654321.```
ops-bot: Resolved notice published to status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/3187654321/resolved — thread closed unless follow-ups requested.
mike: Filed follow-up ticket ENG-4572 for kernel/NFS investigation and to validate autoscaler thresholds.
jen: Thanks team — monitoring for 30m then hand off to infra for postmortem. :white_check_mark:
